config.title: Design DataTable API

intro.title: Design DataTable API
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable DataTable API using React with TypeScript. You'll learn how to design a structured interface that defines the shape of data, columns, and configuration for a table component. The core concept is using TypeScript interfaces and generics to create a type-safe API that ensures your data and table properties are correctly typed. You'll work with key React concepts like props and component structure to make your table flexible and easy to use. By the end, you'll have a clean, maintainable API ready to power a functional data table in your applications.
intro.usecase: DataTable APIs are essential for building enterprise dashboards and admin panels where users need to view, sort, filter, and paginate large datasets. You'll find them in e-commerce platforms displaying product catalogs, financial applications showing transaction histories, and CRM systems listing customer records. As a developer, you'll implement these APIs to handle complex data operations efficiently while providing responsive user interfaces. Mastering DataTable API design enables you to create professional-grade data management interfaces that scale with real-world business needs.

objectives: Define a TypeScript interface to structure the DataTable API with required properties
Apply generic types to create a reusable DataTable component that accepts different data types
Implement a fetchData function to retrieve data from a mock API endpoint
Use React hooks to manage loading, error, and data states within the DataTable component
Construct a table structure with proper HTML elements to display tabular data
Execute conditional rendering to display loading indicators, error messages, or data tables based on state
Utilize array iteration methods to map through data arrays and generate table rows dynamically
Assign appropriate TypeScript types to component props to ensure type safety
Control component behavior by implementing pagination state and handlers
Handle user interactions by implementing sorting functionality on table columns
Modify the API interface to include filtering parameters for data queries
Return a fully functional DataTable component that consumes and displays data from the designed API

steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Add an import statement at the top of your file to import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the standard ES6 import syntax: import { React, useState } from 'react';
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and useState here

// Your component will go below
steps.expectedOutcome: The file will have the necessary React imports to start building a component with state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the useState hook for managing component state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your import syntax. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package using the correct ES6 import format.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import React and useState from the 'react' package to proceed.

steps.title: Create the DataTable component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named DataTable with proper TypeScript typing. The component should return an empty JSX element for now.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function called DataTable that returns JSX. In TypeScript, you can specify the return type as JSX.Element.
steps.expectedOutcome: A DataTable component is defined with TypeScript typing and returns an empty JSX element.
successCriteria: The code should define a component named DataTable (either as a function or arrow function) with proper TypeScript typing that returns JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the DataTable component with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the component is named DataTable and returns JSX with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component definition is missing or incorrect. Create a functional component named DataTable that returns JSX with TypeScript typing.

steps.title: Define the DataTableProps interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named DataTableProps above your DataTable component. Include a required 'data' property (array of any type), a required 'columns' property (array of any type), and an optional 'isLoading' property (boolean).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword to define DataTableProps with the specified properties. Remember to mark 'isLoading' as optional with '?'.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a DataTableProps interface defined with the required data and columns properties and an optional isLoading property.
successCriteria: The interface must be named DataTableProps, include 'data: any[]', 'columns: any[]', and 'isLoading?: boolean'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the DataTableProps interface with all required properties.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your interface includes all three properties: data (array), columns (array), and isLoading (optional boolean).
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition doesn't match the requirements. Check that you've included all required properties with correct types.

steps.title: Define the Column interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named 'Column' with required properties 'key' (string) and 'header' (string), and an optional 'width' property (number).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions. Remember to mark the 'width' property as optional with '?'.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a Column interface that can be used to define table column configurations.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the Column interface with the correct properties. This interface will help structure your table column data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Check that you have all required properties (key, header) and that width is marked as optional with '?'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Column interface isn't defined correctly. Make sure to use the 'interface' keyword and include all required properties with proper TypeScript types.

steps.title: Apply DataTableProps to the component
steps.instruction: In your DataTable component, add the DataTableProps interface as the type for the component's props parameter.
steps.hint: Add a typed parameter to your component function, like (props: DataTableProps) or ({ columns, data }: DataTableProps).
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataTable component should now have a typed props parameter using the DataTableProps interface.
successCriteria: The DataTable component function has a parameter
The parameter is typed with DataTableProps
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully typed your component's props with the DataTableProps interface. This ensures TypeScript will validate that the component receives the correct props structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've properly typed the props parameter with the DataTableProps interface. Check that you're using the interface name exactly as defined.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't seem to have the DataTableProps interface applied to its props parameter. Try adding a parameter to the DataTable function and typing it with DataTableProps.

steps.title: Initialize sort state
steps.instruction: Inside the DataTable component, initialize two state variables using useState: 'sortField' (string) and 'sortDirection' (string). Set their initial values to empty strings.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook twice - once for each state variable. Remember to import useState at the top if it's not already imported.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataTable component will have two state variables: sortField and sortDirection, both initialized as empty strings.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the sort state variables. The component now has sortField and sortDirection state that will help manage table sorting.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you have both state variables: sortField and sortDirection. Both should be typed as strings and initialized with empty strings.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside the DataTable component, use useState to create two state variables: sortField and sortDirection, both initialized as empty strings.

steps.title: Define handleSort function
steps.instruction: Inside the DataTable component, define a handleSort function that takes a column key (string) as a parameter and updates the sort state.
steps.hint: Create a function that accepts a key parameter and calls setSortKey with that key.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleSort function is defined inside the DataTable component that accepts a column key and updates the sort state.
successCriteria: The handleSort function should be defined with a parameter (e.g., columnKey) and call setSortKey with that parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the handleSort function that will update the sort state when called with a column key.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your handleSort function accepts a parameter and calls setSortKey with it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleSort function isn't defined correctly. It should accept a column key parameter and update the sort state using setSortKey.

steps.title: Create sortData helper function
steps.instruction: Inside the DataTable component, create a helper function named sortData that will handle sorting logic. The function should take the data array and sortKey as parameters and return the sorted array.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts data and sortKey parameters, then implement sorting logic inside it. You can use array methods like sort() to sort the data.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a sortData function defined inside your DataTable component that can be used to sort data based on a sort key.
successCriteria: The sortData function should be defined inside the DataTable component, accept parameters for data and sortKey, and return a value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the sortData helper function. This function will be essential for implementing the sorting logic in your DataTable.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the sortData function is defined inside the DataTable component and accepts the required parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sortData function is not properly defined. Remember to create it inside the DataTable component with parameters for data and sortKey.

steps.title: Return the table wrapper
steps.instruction: In the DataTable component's return statement, replace the existing div with a div wrapper that contains a table element. The table should have a basic structure with a thead and tbody.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with a div containing a table element. Inside the table, add a thead and tbody.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataTable component now returns a div containing a table with thead and tbody elements.
successCriteria: return statement contains a div wrapper
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the basic table structure with a wrapper div and table with thead and tbody.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your return statement includes a div wrapper containing a table with both thead and tbody elements.
steps.feedbackWrong: The return statement should be replaced with a div containing a table element that has thead and tbody.

steps.title: Render table headers
steps.instruction: Inside the DataTable component, map through the columns prop to render <th> elements for each column header. Each <th> should display the column's title.
steps.hint: Use the map method on the columns array to create an array of JSX elements. Remember to add a unique key prop to each <th> element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The table headers will be dynamically rendered based on the columns prop, with each column title appearing in its own <th> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully mapped through the columns array to render table headers dynamically. Each header cell now displays the column title with a proper key attribute.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check if you're: 1) using the map method on columns, 2) returning <th> elements, 3) displaying column.title, and 4) adding a key prop using column.key.
steps.feedbackWrong: The table headers aren't rendering correctly. Make sure to map through the columns prop and return <th> elements with the column title and a key attribute.

steps.title: Wire sort handler to headers
steps.instruction: Add onClick handlers to each header cell (<th>) that call the handleSort function with the column's key.
steps.hint: Inside the map function for columns, add onClick={() => handleSort(column.key)} to the <th> element.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of wiring a click handler to a table header
<th onClick={() => handleSort('name')}>Name</th>
steps.expectedOutcome: Each table header cell should have an onClick handler that triggers the sorting logic when clicked.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wired the sort handler to the table headers. Now clicking on any header will trigger the sorting function with the appropriate column key.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure each <th> has an onClick handler that calls handleSort with the column's key property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The table headers don't have the proper click handlers yet. Remember to add onClick={() => handleSort(column.key)} to each <th> element inside the map function.

steps.title: Render table rows with data
steps.instruction: Inside the DataTable component, add a <tbody> element after the <thead> and map through the data array to render table rows with cells for each column.
steps.hint: Use the data prop directly for now (we'll add sorting in the next lesson). For each row, create a <tr> with <td> cells that display the row's value for each column key.
steps.expectedOutcome: The table will display all data rows with proper cells under each column header.
successCriteria: Map through data array to create <tr> elements
Inside each row, map through columns to create <td> elements
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully rendered the table rows with data. The table now displays all the data rows with cells under each corresponding column header.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there are some missing elements. Make sure you've added the <tbody> element and properly mapped through both the data array and columns array to create all table cells.
steps.feedbackWrong: The table rows aren't rendering correctly. Check that you've added the <tbody> element and are mapping through the data array to create table rows with cells for each column.
